## My Reasoning

I've worked this land in Quzhou for more than 40 years. My father worked it before me. I know what this soil wants, I know the weather here, and I know what the village cooperative will take. At my age, I'm not going to start experimenting.

I have 10 mu of contracted land. My son is in Shijiazhuang — he sends money home but he doesn't farm anymore. My wife helps with lighter work. I hire the machine station for planting and harvest because my back can't take what it used to.

I will grow winter wheat and summer maize. That is the rotation here. Everyone does it. The wheat goes in this October after I prepare the soil, comes off in June. Then I turn around immediately and put the corn in on the same ground, harvest it in September before the cold comes. Ten mu, both crops, same fields.

For wheat seed I'll buy Aikang 58 from the village supply station. I've been using it eight or nine years now. It doesn't lodge, it fights off rust reasonably well, and the cooperative buys it without complaint. For maize I'll buy Xianyu 335 hybrid seed — the dealer always has it and my neighbor got over 600 jin per mu last year with it.

Fertilizer — I mix compound fertilizer into the soil as base before planting, then top-dress urea when the wheat is at jointing and again at heading. For the corn I base-fertilize and then top-dress at big bell stage. I know the agricultural station says I use too much nitrogen, but I've seen what happens when you cut back and it rains wrong. I'd rather use a little more and not worry.

Irrigation — I pump from the deep well. Wheat I water four times: once in November to protect the roots from freezing, again at green-up in March, at jointing in April, and at grain fill in May. Corn I water twice — once to get it established and again around tasseling if July is dry, which it often is.

I spray herbicide on both crops early. On the wheat I spray once more in April for powdery mildew, and I watch for aphids in May — if they're bad I spray again. On the corn I spray for stem borer if I see the damage starting.

I use the rotary tiller. Cheaper to hire, faster, and the soil here doesn't need deep ploughing every year in my experience.

I expect about 450 jin — sorry, 450 kg — per mu on the wheat if the spring isn't too dry, and around 550 kg per mu on the maize.
